hints: Focus on how bonding changes across Period 3, from ionic to covalent to molecular.
Remember that $\text{MgO}$ and $\text{Al}_2\text{O}_3$ are giant ionic lattices, while $\text{SiO}_2$ is a giant covalent network.
Look for the oxide that exists as separate small molecules with only weak forces between them, which gives a low melting point.
walkthrough:
**Recall the Period 3 oxide pattern**

Think of the oxides from left to right across Period 3. Bonding moves from giant ionic, to giant covalent, to simple molecular.

Pattern: $\text{Na}_2\text{O}$, $\text{MgO}$, $\text{Al}_2\text{O}_3$ (giant ionic) $\rightarrow$ $\text{SiO}_2$ (giant covalent) $\rightarrow$ $\text{P}_4\text{O}_{10}$, $\text{SO}_2$ (simple molecular)

**Classify the first three oxides**

$\text{MgO}$ has $\text{Mg}^{2+}$ and $\text{O}^{2-}$ ions in a giant lattice with strong ionic bonds. $\text{Al}_2\text{O}_3$ is also giant ionic, with even higher charge. $\text{SiO}_2$ is not ionic at all, it is a giant covalent network of Si-O bonds like diamond.

**Spot the simple molecular oxide**

Phosphorus oxide exists as discrete $\text{P}_4\text{O}_{10}$ molecules. Between the molecules there are only weak van der Waals forces, so it is simple molecular, not giant. That is why it has a much lower melting point and sublimes easily.

options.A: $\text{MgO}$ is a giant ionic lattice of $\text{Mg}^{2+}$ and $\text{O}^{2-}$ ions held by strong ionic bonds in all directions, so it has a very high melting point, not a simple structure.
options.B: $\text{Al}_2\text{O}_3$ is a giant ionic lattice with highly charged $\text{Al}^{3+}$ ions, giving very strong ionic bonding and a very high melting point, not a simple molecular structure.
options.C: $\text{SiO}_2$ is a giant covalent (macromolecular) network where each Si is bonded to four O atoms. This is a common trap because it looks covalent, but it is still giant, with a very high melting point.
options.D: $\text{P}_4\text{O}_{10}$ exists as separate, discrete molecules held together only by weak van der Waals forces. This is a simple molecular structure, so it melts and sublimes at low temperatures compared to the giant structures.
